answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so voting influence depends on paths from trusted seeds rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster with few links to the honest graph has a sparse external cut and low conductance; spectral and min-cut bounds then limit how much seed-reachable voting weight it can accumulate. This remains true even if its members form a dense crystal-like knoll surrounded by an ocean of mutually reinforcing attestations.
